loader_rules.D6_disappearances: a member PERMNO with a crsp_stkdelists row whose price path ends before the last calendar row; effective_date = the calendar row after the last valued row, but never before the dlydelflg = 'Y' row date: when rows without a value lie between the last valued row and the 'Y' row, the event is effective on the first calendar row on or after the 'Y' row date and the position is held at its last value across the gap (amended by card_loader_fix_r1.md item 3, loader review GPT-M3); known_at = effective_date; delisting_return 0.0 when the CIZ delisting return is in the path, NaN when missing (engine default applies); cause cash_merger only for delactiontype MER and delpaymenttype CASH; failure for reasons BKPY, LP, SHLD, INSC, DELQ, FING, INSF, MVOT, MTMK, MVCHI, MVMF or action GLI; else unknown (R4)
loader_rules.D7_split_factors: CIZ cumulative factors fall at a split; the loader checks this on the data and refuses otherwise; only ratios between dates at or before t are used
loader_rules.D8_signal_inputs: daily from crsp_dsf_v2 (prc = |dlyprc|, cfacpr = dlycumfacpr, cfacshr = dlycumfacshr; shrout = the D5 count: the crsp_stkshares count with the latest shrstartdt on or before the row date - 136 calendar days, on the row's basis by the dlycumfacshr ratio, typed missing under the D5 reasons); members from D4; fund_annual from comp_snapshot_csa_pit (known_date = pitdate1); fund_quarterly and announcements from comp_urq; link from ccm_lnkhist; ibes_link from ibes_crsp_link; ibes from ibes_statsumu_epsus; index_daily from INDNO 1000200; a row with no known date or no fiscal key is dropped and counted by table
loader_rules.D9_seal: the loader refuses any sealed path; tilt_frames refuses a window across the seal
loader_rules.P1_path_break: a return whose dlyprevdt is a row with a price and no return is not in the path and is not filled; tilt_frames marks the next row in path_break; the driver blanks each level window (a price ratio or a maximum) that holds one. Holding months (amendment 1, V6). A book holds a position across a path_break row when its weight held at the previous valid row (the last row with a return before the break), after any trade on that row, is not zero. halt_gap_return_v1 then keeps the position to the path_break row, and there the engine books only the return after the break. Each holding month with a row after the previous valid row and on or before the path_break row is a blank month with the reason path_break_held (m55_criteria.BLANK_REASONS). A break that spans a month end blanks every month it touches. Each run has one blank set per period. The driver finds it from that run's loader path_break panel and its engine holdings at each row, never from a book return. Every book holds only names that CW-PIT holds, so the set is that of the CW-PIT book, and the pre-tilt look can use it. Each comparison declares the months of the set that lie inside its own span (from the first to the last month that its period gives it); a check-gap month is never declared. The check declaration joins the sets of the pre-seal and post-seal runs. The declaration covers every book and the benchmark of the comparison (SPY; vwretd in the screen report and the pre-tilt look), so no series of a comparison has a row for a blank month; primary_decision takes one confirm and one check declaration. No value is filled, and an undeclared missing month still refuses. Criteria statistics use the months with values in time order. The HAC t treats the months on each side of a blank month as adjacent; bootstrap blocks run over the months with values; the drawdown path joins the months on each side; the 36-month screen minimum counts the months with values. Every criteria output is appended with its declaration (blank_months and blank_reason_counts in the record; the shortlist digest covers them). Source: docs/decision_log.md 'Declared Blank Months in the Criteria' (1a70eb7)

universe_and_timing.universe: point-in-time S&P 500 members from crsp_dsp500list_v2, identity by PERMNO, priced at r - 1; a member with me_missing (unmapped, ambiguous, multi_class, no_share_fact, stale_share_fact) or unpriced leaves both books at that rebalance; SPY keeps it, so it is replication error (R2, R6)
universe_and_timing.timing_contract: after_close_signal_next_observed_close_v1: at each month-end rebalance row r, cap weights, scores, eligibility, and the TE covariance use rows up to r - 1 only; both books trade at the close of row r and earn from row r + 1
universe_and_timing.rebalance: monthly; the last calendar row of each month in [start, end], without the anchor start; the first rebalance earns from the next month; monthly returns compound measured daily returns by calendar month
universe_and_timing.event_known_at_rule: a disappearance changes the target at r only when its known_at is at or before r - 1
universe_and_timing.b2_rule: The traded set at r is the target members minus the names that settle at r on an event first known at r; their held positions settle under R4 in both books. Scores, ranks, and the covariance stay at r - 1, and these names still count in the ranks of the others. CW-PIT renormalizes pro rata over the traded set; TILT (and the low-risk book) runs the same tilt, cap, and TE step on the traded set. Reported per rebalance: unknown_event_excluded and unknown_event_cw_share (over the r - 1 ME of all target members). A rebalance with no traded member refuses (traded_set_empty). An earlier known_at only with real evidence; no loader invents one.

cw_pit.definition: b = cap weight from D5 market equity at r - 1 over the traded set

tilt.score: each signal is a percentile rank at row r - 1 with its declared sign (higher is better; the engine applies no sign); c = mean of (2u - 1) over the declared signal set; ties take the average rank; ranks are exact fractions; the rank pool is the book members with a valid value
tilt.weight: w = b x (1 + TILT_STRENGTH x c), TILT_STRENGTH = 0.5
tilt.te_target: ex-ante TE against CW-PIT <= 0.02 a year (TE_TARGET)
tilt.te_estimate: sqrt(252) x the ddof-1 standard deviation of the daily active return over the 252 rows ending at r - 1 (COV_ROWS = 252)
tilt.loop: tilt; cap; renormalize multiplicatively on the members free to tilt; repeat to max |w - b| <= cap + 1e-12 (CAP_TOLERANCE) in at most 100 passes (RENORMALIZE_LOOPS), else refuse; then scale w = b + s (w - b), s = min(1, 0.02 / TE); members pinned at b stay at b; TE_TOLERANCE 1e-9; BUDGET_TOLERANCE 1e-12
tilt.short_history: a member without a complete 252-row return window ending at r - 1 gets c = 0 and stays at b
tilt.min_valid: c = 0 when fewer than min_valid declared signals are valid; c = 0 is counted (c_zero_few_signals)
tilt.invalid_values: an infinite signal value refuses; a NaN is invalid for that signal only

Amendment 2: test B is stopped at the coverage stop (primary_family.test_B.after_coverage_stop), so the low-risk book gets no g, no engine call, and no return in any period (screen, confirm, and check), the last_close rerun included
low_risk.construction: power volatility tilt (a'): m_i = (s_i / s_med)^(-g); renormalize the free weights b m to the free cap weight; cap |w - b| at LOWRISK_CAP = 0.02 and renormalize until the cap holds (refuse after the loop limit); scale active weights down until ex-ante TE <= LOWRISK_TE = 0.05
low_risk.s_i: ddof-1 standard deviation of the 252 daily simple returns ending at r - 1; a member without a full window is pinned at w = b and counted
low_risk.s_med: median over the target members with a full window, the B2 excluded names included
low_risk.costs_events_halts: same as the tilt: R8 at 1x and 2x, R4 events, halt policy; runs through run_book

calibration.knob: g only; cap 0.02 and TE 0.05 are fixed hard limits
calibration.target: LOWRISK_TARGET_RATIO = 0.87: median over screen rebalances (1963-07 to 1992-12) of the ex-ante whole-book volatility ratio to CW-PIT
calibration.ratio: the traded book on its complete-case rows, without its gap members (amendment 1, V2). A gap is a missing return in the 252-row window ending at r - 1 after the member's first-ever return (the short flag of rebalance_members decides, not the first return inside the window). A traded member with a gap is left out of both books in the ratio at that rebalance, typed as a gap member and counted (ratio_gap_members, ratio_gap_cw_share); it has no full window, so it is pinned at w = b and no weight changes. The other members are measured at their book weights on the rows where each of them has a return, so only leading rows (before a member's first-ever return) remove rows (ratio_rows_leading). At least LOWRISK_RATIO_MIN_ROWS = 126 rows, else ratio_window_short; status defined_full (252 rows) or defined_partial; no fill, clip, or repair. Source: docs/decision_log.md 'Gap Members Leave the Low-Risk Ratio' (cebb487)
calibration.choice: two-sided median bracket: undefined rebalances enter the median once at +inf and once at -inf; each g meets, fails, or is ambiguous. Order: a refusal below the first g that meets stops; then ratio_coverage_low (undefined share above LOWRISK_UNDEFINED_MAX = 0.10); then ratio_coverage_ambiguous (an ambiguous g below the first g that meets; the owner decides); then chosen (the first g that meets); else no_g_reaches_target (stop and ask the owner; the budget is not loosened)
calibration.window_diagnostic: treat every defined_partial rebalance as undefined and repeat the bracket classes and the choice without the coverage stop; window_sensitive only when that choice differs from the main decision; window_diag_coverage_high (diagnostic undefined share above 0.10) recorded apart. A gap member left out of the ratio does not make a rebalance defined_partial, so this diagnostic does not cover gap rebalances; they are reported apart (reports_owed.low_risk_r6; amendment 1, V2)
calibration.inputs: second moments only, ex-ante only; no realized portfolio volatility, mean return, Sharpe ratio, return gap, or realized portfolio return is computed
calibration.logged_per_g: every grid value with the share of rebalances where the cap binds, the TE scale is below 1, and members are pinned (R9)
calibration.order: coordinator default (logged): the calibration rule is frozen in this file first and the calibration runs after the freeze; this is stricter than the O-20 order (calibrate before the freeze); the calibration runs once, on the tilt_frames(run="primary") panel, and every engine call of the low-risk book, the last_close rerun included, uses its chosen g (books.disappearance_r4.last_close_rerun)

costs.basis: one way, per traded notional, commission + spread bp, dated
costs.which_schedule: screen runs use SCREEN_COST_SCHEDULE only (no half-spread override); confirm and check runs use COST_SCHEDULE, which equals it from 1993-01-01, with the half-spread override
costs.half_spread_override: Confirm and check runs only, in every book (CW-PIT too), per stock and rebalance row r: a trade at row r pays a spread of scale x max(the spread of the dated schedule at r, the CRSP closing half-spread at r - 1), so the 2x case doubles the result; the commission stays per row, and on a halt-locked row the full row cost applies (H-3c). The half-spread is 10,000 x (ask - bid) / (ask + bid) in bp, from dlybid and dlyask of the PERMNO on the calendar row r - 1: the midpoint is the basis of the close that the engine trades at, and a locked quote gives 0. A cell is invalid for the first reason that applies: no_quote_row, quote_missing (both sides missing), quote_one_sided, quote_nonpositive (a side at 0 or below), quote_crossed (ask below bid). An invalid cell keeps its reason, pays the schedule spread, and is counted (R6). Days with dlyprcflg = 'BA' are valid (OI-11). No value is clipped. One-pull rule (amendment 3): the quote files are those of one run of coord/reports/m6_prep/wrds_pull_quotes.py (code_pins) into a folder named wrds_quotes_*, under the O-22 seal rule; a re-pull is a stop for the owner. reports/wrds_quotes_manifest_2025.json (file names, rows, SHA-256, and vintage; no row) is committed before run 3. The driver reads the quote main files only after it checks each one against that manifest. It refuses when the manifest is missing, when a hash or a row count differs, when the vintage is not data.vintage, when a path is under sealed/, when a quote row is dated in the seal window [2019-07-31, 2020-07-31), when a (PERMNO, date) repeats, and when a quote row has no main daily row of the first pull on (permno, dlycaldt). The quote file hashes enter data_files_sha256 in every stage context. The confirm run does not start before that pull.
costs.split: the dated rate is split between the engine's transaction and slippage columns; annual turnover and cost drag include the first purchase from cash
costs.no_switch_cost: long only with fixed signal weights; no switch cost; no borrow cost (no shorts)

disappearance_r4.rule: one event set for both books; CRSP delisting return in the path when present; without it, last close for a cash merger and -100 percent otherwise (long only); timing in both modes: no settlement happens before the dlydelflg = 'Y' row date; when rows without a value lie between the last valued row and the 'Y' row, the event is effective and known on the first calendar row on or after the 'Y' row date

disappearance_r4.last_close_rerun: the all-events R4 rerun uses the loader last_close mode: the return of every dlydelflg = 'Y' row is removed from the price path, so the path ends at the last trade close, and every event settles at that close (delisting_return = 0.0); no settlement happens before the 'Y' row date. The engine event-mode switch (EVENT_RUNS last_close) alone is not this rerun. Two engine calls (amendment 1, V1): the primary run is an engine call on tilt_frames(run="primary") with its primary event run; the rerun is a second engine call on tilt_frames(run="last_close") with its last_close event run. The engine's single-call fragility flags (fragile_active_sign and fragile_lowrisk_active_sign) are never reported: in one call both event runs use one price path, and they compare against CW-PIT only. The low-risk book is calibrated once, on the tilt_frames(run="primary") panel; both engine calls (primary and last_close) use that calibration's chosen g, and the last_close call never recalibrates

list.name: 3-month FY1 EPS revision / price
list.definition: 3 x the mean of the valid one-month FY1 revisions of the last three statistics months (at least 2); each revision = (FY1 mean at month m - FY1 mean at m - 1) / price at the m - 1 month end, one share basis
list.source_data: IBES unadjusted summary, CRSP split factors, same FPEDATS
list.usable_from: the first month-end row after the statistics date

list.name: earnings surprise, seasonal random walk
list.definition: (EPS q - EPS q-4) / sd of the eight prior such differences (at least 6), first-reported EPS, on the cfacshr share basis of q (P-9 option (a))
list.history_rule: an S2 quarter is read only when the PERMNO has a cfacshr row at the basis date (the known date) and at rdq, each an as-of read at most one month old, and the two factors are equal within a relative tolerance of 1e-9 and an absolute tolerance of 0 (amendment 1, V3; np.isclose(at_rdq, f, rtol=1e-9, atol=0.0), that is |factor at rdq - factor at the basis date| <= 1e-9 x |factor at the basis date|). When they differ (a cfacshr change, such as a split or a stock dividend, after rdq and on or before the known date), the quarter is split_in_basis_window: q or q - 4 gives that reason, and a prior quarter drops each difference it enters, as a missing prior quarter does. When the read at rdq fails, the quarter gets that read's own reason (stale, no_market_data, missing_item, or invalid_value). A factor read on or after the seal start from a row before it gives no_market_data (stale when that row is more than one month old). So a quarter with rdq from 2019-07-31 to 2020-08-02 (no main daily row on those dates) has no value whatever its known date, because its rdq read gives no_market_data or stale. When signals are built per seal segment, the post-seal segment has no daily row before 2020-08-03, so any quarter with rdq before that date gives no_market_data there. Amendment 1 adds the case with a known date on or after 2020-08-03, where the basis read alone succeeds. A new listing has no S2 value for about 2.5 to 3 years. Source: docs/decision_log.md 'Unknown Share Bases Are Typed Missing' item 2 (312d284)

list.name: announcement return, days -1 to +1

list.name: accruals
list.definition: ((d act - d che) - (d lct - d dlc - d txp) - dp) / mean(at, at lag)

list.name: net share issuance, 12 months
list.definition: log(shrout x cfacshr at the month-end anchor before t's month) - log(the same 12 months earlier); shrout is the D5 count (D8): the latest shrstartdt on or before the anchor date - 136 calendar days, on the anchor row's basis

list.name: book-to-market

limitations: Point-in-time Compustat (Snapshot) starts about 1986-12, so S2, S4, S5, S6, and S8 have about five screen years (1987 to 1992) before the backfill and 6-month lags. S3 needs eight known quarters with RDQ from comp_urq, so its screen may be short too; the real-start rule handles it. S1 (IBES from 1976) and S7 are not affected by this; S7 still loses coverage from the unseen share basis (screen months up to 1964-06) and the seal (check months 2021-09 to 2022-01), see data.loader_rules.D5_market_equity and limitations[9]. The confirm period is fully covered. Source: decision log 'Signal-Screen Criteria Module', WRDS source facts; card_loader.md D8; coord/reports/m55_trial/card_trial_fix_r1.md item 11.

Survivor and drop bias: a member with me_missing or no price leaves both books; on real_v2 step 4b, 6.37 percent of pre member-days were unmapped but 9.49 percent for later delisting candidates, so the drop removes more later failures and biases both books up. CRSP intake at 312d284 (the pinned loader): unmapped member-days are 18,519 of 423,341 for later failures against 18,776 of 2,967,375 for current members. Nearly all of the rise from the intake at 0c60805 (159,791 of 159,957 member-days) is the basis_unseen data_start case in 1961 to 1963 (data.loader_rules.D5_market_equity), before the first screen rebalance; the other 166 are the seal case in 2020. Source: index_tilt_design_note.md section 1; coordinator intakes at 312d284 and 0c60805.

Backfill bias: Compustat signals need two fiscal years known at t (S2 and S3 eight quarters); S2 needs CRSP history at the basis date, so new listings have no S2 value for about 2.5 to 3 years, which favors seasoned firms. Source: signal_screen_design_note.md section 3; decision log 'Signals S1 to S8 Rules'.

Low power: rule A detects about 0.72 percent a year at 50 percent power and 1.08 at 80 percent over 254 months at 2 percent realized TE; an IR of 0.3 (0.6 percent a year) is found about 39 percent of the time, about 30 percent under Holm with two tests; the two-sided BY family of 2 detects about 1.0 to 1.4 percent a year. 'A not met' often means 'not shown'. Source: signal_screen_design_note.md section 7; index_tilt_design_note.md appendix; O-20.

The half-spread override needs CRSP closing bid and ask, which the first pull did not include; the screen runs without it, and the confirm run waits for the owner's second WRDS pull. Source: RESUME.md section 0h backlog; coord/reports/m55_trial/card_trial_defaults.md item 3.

Test B: an ex-ante ratio near 0.87 gives a beta near 0.88, which under a 5 to 6 percent equity premium predicts a return gap of about 0.6 to 0.7 point a year, past the 0.5 margin; B passes only if the low-risk effect pays about one point a year in 1993-2014. Source: low_risk_design_note.md section 3.

A defined_partial low-risk ratio cannot measure risk on rows before a member existed; such windows are declared, counted (ratio_rows_leading counts the rows removed), and checked by window_sensitive. At a rebalance with a gap member, the ratio is that of the book without that member (a sub-book), so it moves toward the ratio of the free members by an amount that grows with the member's cap weight and risk; window_sensitive does not check it; the count of gap rebalances and the maximum ratio_gap_cw_share are reported. Source: expert_decision.md, residual limitation; amendment 1, V2 (docs/decision_log.md 'Gap Members Leave the Low-Risk Ratio', cebb487).

Factor-level reuse: the signals come from papers on these months and M5 step 2 screened factor returns built from the same stocks; results are 'stock-level out-of-sample, factor-level in-sample'. Source: O-17 Q3.
CW-PIT uses full market cap, while S&P used float cap from 2005; with the me_missing drops and SPY's fee, CW-PIT - SPY is replication error. Source: index_tilt_design_note.md section 2.

Seal: the check period leaves out CHECK_GAP_MONTHS 2019-07 to 2021-08 (26 months): the seal holding months, 2020-08 (the 2020-07-31 row that would form it is sealed; the first month-end row after the seal is 2020-08-31, but the post-seal segment is anchored at 2021-07-30), and the warm-up to the first month end with a full 252-row window (2021-08-31; 251 post-seal rows on 2021-07-30, 273 on 2021-08-31); windows that touch the seal stay typed missing; the post-seal engine segment starts at the anchor 2021-07-30 (first rebalance 2021-08-31, first labelled month 2021-09), and signals are built once per seal segment. S7 has no 12-month-earlier anchor for the check month 2021-09 (no calendar row in 2020-07), so no member has an S7 value in that month (short_history, unless the read at the 2021-07-30 anchor gives its own reason). S2 is typed missing for all or nearly all members in the post-seal check months to about the first half of 2023, because q - 4 or too many of the prior quarters have rdq before 2020-08-03; in those months a book on S2 alone equals CW-PIT (c = 0), and the by-month report gives the share. Source: O-12, O-18, O-22; coord/reports/m55_trial/card_trial_fix_r1.md item 13 (Round 2 Decision, R2-M1); amendment 1, V4 (loader review Opus A-1; check-gap review advisory A2).
The seal does not stop price levels on both sides from implying the net change across it; no script computes it. Source: wrds_pull.py docstring, residual limits.
WRDS tables without a price or a return keep seal-dated rows in their main files. Source: O-22.
Low-risk bootstrap percentile bound is slightly liberal (about 6 to 7 percent size at a true ratio of 1.0). Source: decision log 'Signal-Screen Criteria Module' default 3.
The pre-1993 benchmark vwretd is gross of fund fees, so it sits above an investable fund. Source: coord/reports/m55_trial/card_trial_defaults.md item 2.
